title: Multi-Scale Simulations of Ionic Charge Carriers in Solid State Ionic Materials for Electrochemical Energy Conversions
abstract:
<jats:p>In solid state ionic conductors, the defects (or ionic and electronic charge carriers) related thermodynamic and kinetic properties can only be modeled in a multi-scale simulation way.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    In this talk, I am going to summarize my computational efforts over a decade on the multi-scale simulations of this family of materials in the following order:
                    <jats:list list-type="roman-lower">
                      <jats:list-item>
                        <jats:p>
                          My master's thesis at Penn State with Prof. Zi-Kui Liu on CALPHAD (CALculation of PHAse Diagram) modeling of defect chemistry and phase stability (La,Sr)CoO
                          <jats:italic>3-δ</jats:italic>
                          , a pure classical thermodynamic description with
                          <jats:italic>ab-initio</jats:italic>
                          and experimental thermochemical data as the aid.
                        </jats:p>
                      </jats:list-item>
                      <jats:list-item>
                        <jats:p>
                          My PhD work with Prof. Meilin Liu at Georgia Tech about the oxygen ion and proton transport in Y-doped BaZrO
                          <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                          using Reactive Force Field Molecular Dynamics simulations, with edge-dislocation inside the bulk lattice.
                        </jats:p>
                      </jats:list-item>
                      <jats:list-item>
                        <jats:p>
                          My independent work on an
                          <jats:italic>ab-initio</jats:italic>
                          thermodynamic and kinetic model of estimating proton conductivity in order to select optimal dopant in BaHfO3.
                        </jats:p>
                      </jats:list-item>
                      <jats:list-item>
                        <jats:p>My independent work on an statistical thermodynamic treatment of lattice defects (i.e. aliovalent dopants and oxygen vacancies) in BaZrO3 to study defect-clustering and degradation of this proton conductor.</jats:p>
                      </jats:list-item>
                      <jats:list-item>
                        <jats:p>Lastly, I will talk about the epitaxial and interfacial strain effect on the Ce3+ polaron and oxygen vacancy distribution over CeO2 (111) surface and oxygen ion conductivity within the SDC/BZY hetero-interface.</jats:p>
                      </jats:list-item>
                    </jats:list>
                  </jats:p>
